summary:
Mission Echo is an interactive, browser-based educational platform developed by team 00Tea-Minus for the "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge. Primarily designed for children aged 10–12 (while also supporting ages 8–10 and 12+), it brings six historic NASA missions across the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space back to life: Apollo 15 LRV-1, Apollo 12 ALSEP, Spirit & Opportunity, Ingenuity, Pioneer 10, and the Kepler Space Telescope.

Instead of reading dense technical archives, learners explore an interactive Solar System map, experience voice-narrated four-chapter mission stories paired with authentic NASA media, test spacecraft components in a simplified Environmental Test Chamber, send speed-of-light radio pings, and play six custom educational mini-games.

By connecting real NASA mission data with hands-on engineering challenges and storytelling, Mission Echo transforms silent off-world artifacts into engaging lessons that inspire the next generation of space explorers.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Mission Echo is an interactive, browser-based NASA space-hardware museum and engineering playground built by team 00Tea-Minus for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge (Abandoned but Not Forgotten). It brings six historic NASA missions across three exploration regions back to life:

  • Moon: Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-1) and Apollo 12 ALSEP Science Station
  • Mars: Spirit & Opportunity Rovers and the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
  • Deep Space: Pioneer 10 and the Kepler Space Telescope

Users start on an Interactive Solar System Map to select a destination and explore each spacecraft through four core experiences:

  1. Mission Story & Voice Mode: Four-chapter narratives pairing authentic NASA archival media with optional browser-based narration (Web Speech API) and direct links to official NASA NSSDCA and NASA Science mission pages.
  2. Interactive Blueprint Lab & Environmental Test Chamber: Learners inspect real spacecraft components, assemble hardware using suitable parts, and run simplified environmental failure tests (extreme cold, thin Martian atmosphere, dust, or power loss) to see why incorrect designs fail.
  3. Six Original Mini-Games: Custom HTML5 Canvas 2D interactive activities tailored to each machine's engineering challenges (e.g., unfolding and driving the lunar buggy, spinning Ingenuity's rotors in Mars's thin air, or detecting exoplanet transits).
  4. Light-Speed Communication Simulator: Users send a simulated radio signal from Earth and observe representative one-way light-speed travel times (~299,792 km/s) across the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space.

Progress, Mission Quizzes, and a customizable astronaut avatar shop are saved locally in the browser—requiring zero installation, login, or accounts.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Primary Audience (Ages 10–12) & Multi-Age Accessibility: Designed so younger learners (8–10) can explore visually through animations and mini-games, 10–12-year-olds connect mission history with hands-on engineering decisions, and older students (12+) can follow direct links to primary NASA scientific sources.
  • Classroom & Home Ready: Runs on any modern browser as a free, zero-friction educational activity for teachers, parents, and students.
  • Scientific & Media Literacy: Authentic NASA photos, videos, simulations, and artist concepts are explicitly labeled (REAL NASA PHOTO, REAL NASA VIDEO, NASA SIMULATION, NASA ARTIST CONCEPT), teaching students to distinguish archival evidence from illustrations.

Tools, Technologies & Resources Used

  • Frontend & Core Stack: React 18, TypeScript 5, Vite 5, Tailwind CSS 3
  • Interactive Graphics & Audio: HTML5 Canvas 2D (custom physics and mini-games), Web Speech API (Voice Mode narration), Web Audio API (synthesized UI/game sound effects), Browser localStorage (client-side progress persistence)
  • Hosting & Version Control: Vercel (live web app) and GitHub (https://github.com/talattofc/Abandoned-but-not-forgotten-00Tea-Minus)
  • Scientific Data Sources: Official NASA Science mission pages and the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA)
  • AI Usage & Transparency: AI coding and image-generation tools were used to accelerate development and create stylized pixel-art/sprite assets; all AI-assisted visuals are clearly distinguished from authentic NASA archival material.

Creativity & Factors Considered

  • Learning Through Failure: Instead of passive fact cards, the Blueprint Lab lets students test wrong parts and visually observe why rubber tires freeze on the Moon or standard blades cannot lift off on Mars.
  • Respecting Real Physics (Simplified for Education): Simulations and light-speed delays are grounded in real mission constraints while remaining approachable for 10–12-year-olds.
  • Zero-Barrier Access: No backend, no account creation, and lightweight client-side architecture ensure anyone—including schools with restricted networks—can launch and explore immediately.
